text:
Nina: heads up — onboarding sample app using the Python SDK fails on createDeployment. API returns 400: "invalid value for public" even though curl works.
Liam: ugh again. paste the curl + sdk call?
Nina: curl that works:
```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/deployments \
  -d '{"name":"test","public":true}'
```
Nina: Python SDK (failing):
```py
client.admin.create_deployment(name='test', public=True)
# raises: HTTPError 400: {"error":"invalid value for public"}
```
Ravi: Did you inspect the outbound payload?
Nina: Yep. SDK is sending `{"name":"test","public":"true"}` — public is string.
Liam: ah, stringified booleans. We added safe-json encoder for some nested types and it coerces bool -> str in 1.4.0.
Pat: That explains why backend started rejecting it after we switched to strict schema validation last week. Previously schema accepted "true" as boolean-like.
Jo: Workaround: pass raw body: `client.request('POST','/v1/admin/deployments', json={'name':'test','public':True})` or downgrade to 1.3.x for now.
sdk-ci: Created issue #3561 - "python-sdk: boolean params serialized as strings in safe-json encoder" and triggered flaky-tests job.
Ravi: I can put up a hotfix to ensure booleans are preserved in the encoder, plus add a unit test.
Nina: Please also add an integration test that posts to /admin/deployments with true/false values. This blocks sampleapp onboarding.
Liam: will add changelog and notify support so new onboarding runs don't hit customers.
Pat: We should also audit other primitive types (ints/floats/null) — might be similar.
Nina: Thanks all — workaround applied and sampleapp now proceeds. :thumbsup:
Jo: tagging devex board: sdk-serialization.
Liam: will backport to 1.4.1 after review.
